items.basis: The proposed adaptive EMF tuning mechanism relies on real-time sensing and machine learning algorithms to optimize scaling pathways, but the candidate fails to provide a clear explanation of how these algorithms will be trained and validated, particularly in the context of variable water compositions and environmental conditions. The lack of a detailed algorithmic framework and training data raises significant concerns about the mechanism's ability to adapt and optimize scaling pathways effectively.

The candidate's predicted effect of reducing adherent and soluble scaling species by 20% is based on a 6-month pilot-scale test, but the boundary conditions of this test are not clearly defined. Specifically, the candidate does not provide information on the range of water compositions and environmental conditions that will be tested, nor does it specify the duration of the test or the number of test runs. Without clear boundary conditions, it is impossible to evaluate the validity of the predicted effect.

The candidate cites [doi:10.1038/s41545-026-00565-8] as evidence that EMF tuning can control scaling pathways, but this study only investigated the effects of EMF tuning on CaCO3 and CaSO4•2H2O scaling in a controlled laboratory setting. The candidate's proposed mechanism, however, involves real-time sensing and machine learning algorithms, which are not addressed in the cited study. Furthermore, the study did not investigate the effects of variable water compositions and environmental conditions, which are critical to the candidate's proposed mechanism.

The candidate's predicted effect of maintaining a normalized permeate flux above 90% for 12 months without chemical antiscalant dosing or acid injection is equivalent to the baseline, which is the current implementation of the brackish-water reverse-osmosis desalination skid. The candidate fails to provide any evidence that its proposed mechanism will outperform the baseline, and the predicted effect is not supported by any concrete data or analysis.

Without clear measurement protocols, it is difficult to evaluate the validity of the predicted effect.
